text: sealed at aec2e4bedade16cab5edcbb54aab5c2da3db3510; seal-time probe script metric=6 target=0 measuring=true

seal.statement: A deterministic five-node cold-formation simulator on the in-process path - virtual clock, seeded in-memory transport, a discrete-event scheduler charging each node's virtual time per owner from the committed calibration table, real owners throughout, and a guard that throws on any ambient clock or timer read in deterministic mode - reproduces the seed-starvation signature of main (seed gap fraction at least 50 percent with every joiner under 5 percent, incomplete-lease observations naming all five nodes with escalating backoff, prioritySpreadGap non-decreasing with zero operations in flight, admission ending in control_plane_pressure), two runs of one seed produce byte-identical reports, the signature holds across a 0.5x-2x one-dimensional sweep of every coefficient, a run completes in under 60 seconds of real time, and a live report plus its log archive can be ingested as a canonical scenario.

text: Calibration-to-coefficient gap: the design's cost table (test/simulation/calibration/formation-seed-2026-09-05.json) wants four work keys with input-unit denominators - raft_entries_applied per committed entry, priority_planning_pass per pass, control_snapshot_build per build, membership_publication_reconcile per reconcile - but the accepted run measured per-owner turn segments: raft_protocol 14.5 us per segment over 3.4 M segments, raft_apply 318 us over 24.7 k, rebalancer 111 us over 340 k, membership_publication 57 us over 415 k, readiness 1.9 ms over 330, admin 70 us over 45 k (seed-owner-costs.md). The seed log carries no per-pass or per-build counters (0 'planning pass', 0 'snapshot built' lines; 134 'committed', 124 'reconcile' mentions). The simulator's scheduler therefore charges per owner dispatch (cost per segment, segment rate driven by the model), which the design already frames as the seam charge surface; the four work keys map onto owners (raft_apply, rebalancer+readiness, admin, membership_publication) and the coefficient file records the segment basis with the run's digests as provenance. Recorded before any coefficient is authored.

The probe is the file the epic authorizes (scripts/checks/formation-sim-reproduces.js): it runs the simulator entry test/simulation/formation-sim-runner.js twice in temporary directories and counts unmet reproduction conditions (identical hashes, the four signature predicates, under 60 s); with no runner in the tree it reads 6. The simulator is in-process and deterministic (no network, no child processes, no wall clock), so the probe starts nothing live (R27).

Altitude check at the start: the substrate exists and is reused, not rebuilt - createVirtualNetwork (test/distributed/harness/virtual-network.js: seeded in-memory transport, one event queue, per-node clocks, chargeNode single-core serialisation, networkTimeSource per node), createCostTable (cost-table.js; unknown keys cost zero, so the runner validates first), SeededRandomSource + PctScheduler, connectRaftCluster/driveNetwork hosting real LifeRaft over the network (raft-network-host.js), createNodeHosts (membership-consistency helpers) as the per-node real-owner wiring template, hostedInteractions from owner-interaction-model.js as the sealed real-owner surface, the attribution seam with an injected microsecond clock, and deriveFormationVerdict as a pure function over synthesised inputs. About twenty formation-path modules already take a TimeSource. What has no seam: src/bootstrap (188 Date.now, 17 setTimeout, 6 setInterval, no resolveTimeSource), src/transport (69/18/4), and the gap watchdog that feeds seedGaps. Cold formation is bootstrap-dominated, so the quest is a sequence of bounded seam commits; the simulator is built up in slices that each move the probe.

Slice order (decision): (1) the runner skeleton under test/simulation - five nodes on createVirtualNetwork with real LifeRaft cohorts, per-node charging from a committed coefficient file derived from the calibration table (segment basis), the attribution seam on the network clock, the deterministic-mode guard, atomic sorted report through deriveFormationVerdict with formationMetrics - which settles the determinism and report conditions (probe 6 to 4); (2) real readiness/publication/rebalancer hosts per node via createNodeHosts on the network clock; (3) bootstrap seams, one bounded commit each with a red-on-revert test, starting where the design names them (bootstrap-node-ready-rebalance-owner, unified-rebalancer initial scheduling); (4) the signature, then the 0.5x-2x sweep; (5) ingestion. No slice adds a script beyond the authorized probe.

Slice 1 first run: with six priority-table groups and heartbeat-only Raft traffic the seed sees 97 raft_protocol segments per second against 22,560 per second in the calibration (the live seed leads every system-table replica group and carries appends, not only heartbeats). Formation over the virtual network completes 45 ms after the fifth join; two runs of one seed hash identical; a run takes 0.2 s. The group set must become a scenario datum sized from the real bootstrap's system partitions in the slice that hosts bootstrap; LifeRaft ran clean under the deterministic guard (no ambient read on its timer or packet path).

Slice 1 under test/simulation: coefficient file formation-seed-2026-09-13.json derived from the calibration evidence on a segment basis with provenance (head, evidence, report sha256); loader that refuses calibration_missing/invalid/source_unbound and builds the cost table keyed owner:<name>; deterministic guard (Date.now, performance.now, setTimeout/setInterval/setImmediate throw nondeterministic_owner_seam inside a tagged dispatch, restored after); per-node per-owner charge accumulator that charges whole virtual milliseconds through the network time source and records gaps at the 1 s threshold; staged real-LifeRaft cohorts (seed alone, joiners admitted on the join schedule; inbound packets and Raft timer fires are raft_protocol segments under the guard); runner with five nodes, six priority-table groups, joins at 5/10/15/20 s, formed when every group's members know one leader; report in the live shape with formationMetrics and the verdict from deriveFormationVerdict over a synthesised seed log, sorted keys, virtual timestamp, atomic write. Probe 6 to 4: identical hashes and the 60 s bound hold; the four signature predicates wait for the readiness, publication, rebalancer and bootstrap hosts. A subsystem rule maps test/simulation to convergence-topology.

Verifier r1 (subagent): REJECT - (1) gap records overlapped: every charge on a busy node pushed the whole backlog as a fresh gap (11 gaps summing 24.9 s for 2.3 s of work); (2) a literal NUL byte in the charge map key made git treat the file as binary; should-fix: eventLoopGapMs was total busy time while the probe reads it as the watchdog's gap fraction (live: 91.9 percent busy vs 52 percent gap); producer type diverged from the live string; the guard covers only the synchronous prefix of LifeRaft's async handlers and Math.random/process.hrtime sit outside it; the write stub was missing from the adapter contract; advisories: seeded transport nominal (fixed 1 ms links, no loss policy yet), seed promote() at t=0 where production elects, zero-cost owner charge, escalation predicate too loose, analyze-latent-blockers reads summary which the sim report lacks. Verified clean: cost-table rounding exact over 1..200000 ms, no double counting, hashes identical for seeds 1 and 3, no LifeRaft decision reproduced, verdict honest, empty arrays cannot satisfy conditions 3-5, classification rule unique.

Verifier r1 repairs: busy time is tracked as contiguous stretches (a charge on an idle node opens one, on a busy node extends it) and gaps are stretches at or above 1 s, so gap time is bounded by charged time (unit test reproduces the 1200-plus-10 segment case); nodes report busyMs and eventLoopGapMs separately and the probe's gap fraction reads the gap field; the map key uses a visible separator; producer is the string formation-sim; zero-cost owners never reach charge; the escalation predicate requires non-decreasing with one strict increase; the runner header and the adapter contract state the guard's synchronous-prefix scope, the write stub and the fixed-delay lossless links.

Verifier r2 (same subagent): APPROVE - stretches never overlap (independent reproduction: three charges at one instant merge into one stretch; a charge exactly at busyUntil opens a new one, the watchdog's unit), gap fraction now watchdog-style, producer a string, guard scope and adapter contract stated, escalation predicate tightened; new advisory: a hosted owner that charges the network time source directly bypasses the stretch ledger - route slice-2 owner charges through ChargeAccumulator.charge.

Slice 2 map (Explore): createNodeHosts wires the real gateway, readiness service, table policy, storage accounting/admission, membership publication coordinator plus runtime owner, message router host and (separately) the rebalance coordinator; readiness (participation-base 148-157), CDC, the coordinator (now inherited from readiness), the rebalance coordinator (lifecycle 218-226) and storage accounting take an injected clock; the gateway and admission take a now option. Unseamed on the formation path: TablePolicyService (five Date.now reads: table-policy-service.js 181, 201, 338, 467, 504 - src/policy is outside the epic's authorizes) and UnifiedRebalancer's constructor (Date.now plus Math.random jitter at unified-rebalancer-lifecycle-base.js 196-202 despite accepting nowFn and a RandomSource). The lease-wait observation needs no log parsing: getCheckRebalanceBlocker returns the decision whose logContext carries blockerReason, unreadyNodeIds and delayMs before apply() logs. prioritySpreadGap is a harness aggregate: the sum of buildDerivedPriorityPartitionSummary blockedPartitions[].spreadGap; inFlightCount from summarizeReplicaOperationLiveness with nowMs injected. Admission transitions come from buildControlPlaneQuiescenceSnapshot over a nowFn-injected local snapshot builder, which needs replicated services/partitions rows. Cross-node replication: the staged cohort has no commit-apply hook; createReplicaPropagation builds its own network and uses ambient setImmediate, so slice 2 adds a commit-apply hook on the cohort or a network-sharing propagation adapter. Templates: dt6-publication-persist-pipeline-network, dt6-rebalancer-timeout-loop-network, readiness-time-source-seam.

Slice 2a, first bounded seam: UnifiedRebalancer's constructor drew its start jitter and stabilisation anchor from Date.now() and Math.random() although it already accepted nowFn and a RandomSource (unified-rebalancer-lifecycle-base.js 196-202); both now read the owner's own seams (defaults unchanged, byte-identical in production). Red-on-revert test test/rebalancer/unified-rebalancer-start-jitter-seam.test.js proves a virtual clock and a fixed draw determine rebalanceStartAtMs and lastStateChangeTime.

Verifier (subagent): APPROVE on the rebalancer start-jitter seam - nowFn and randomSource are assigned before the changed reads on every constructor path, defaults are byte-identical (unbound Date.now, RealRandomSource = Math.random, same evaluation order), the test is red on revert (10 000 vs a wall-clock value), no other ambient read remains in the file, jitter cannot be NaN from config defaults; four rebalancer suites green. Note: the seam should land as its own commit rather than bundled with the slice files.

Owner decision 2026-09-13: authorizes widens by src/policy so the table policy service gets a clock seam instead of a stand-in; row stamps written to the tables (updated_at) stay on the wall clock per the design's data-stamp decision, only the policy cache TTL reads move to the injected clock.

Slice 2b, second bounded seam: TablePolicyService measures its policy-cache TTL on an injectable now (options.now, default Date.now) at the four cache reads; the updated_at row stamp stays on the wall clock as data. Red-on-revert test test/policy/table-policy-clock-seam.test.js: two reads within the TTL hit the cache, the entry expires exactly at the TTL on the injected clock, and the default clock is Date.now.

Verifier (subagent): APPROVE on the table policy clock seam - exact hunks only, now assigned before any use, no subclass/mixin/mock collision, byte-identical default, red-on-revert proven by executing the test against HEAD's file (not ok at the TTL), TTL from POLICY_DEFAULT 30 000 ms, gateway stub path confirmed, audits clean, four policy suites green (163 assertions).

Slice 2c: every node hosts its real control-plane owners on its network clock (test/simulation/formation-sim-node-hosts.js: gateway, readiness, table policy, storage accounting and admission, publication coordinator plus runtime owner, rebalance coordinator; a real UnifiedRebalancer per priority partition on the seed), node/partition/service rows are scenario data, and owner passes run every 250 ms virtual inside the production attribution seam so the real turn counts of each pass are charged per owner (test/simulation/formation-sim-owner-passes.js). The deterministic guard found, in order, ambient clock reads the design's inventory named: twelve on the rebalancer's planning path (policy scheduler, planning gate, priority readiness, critical topology) now on nowFn; the startup recovery coordinator constructed without a clock in both the rebalance coordinator and the rebalancer fallback, now on their clocks; the readiness planning version key defaulting to Date.now, now the service's clock; and the gap watchdog's sync-section registry stamping performance.now, now an injectable clock (configureSharedSyncSectionClock, measurement only). Red-on-revert test test/rebalancer/unified-rebalancer-planning-clock-seam.test.js replaces the ambient clock by a thrower for a whole awaited planning-gate pass. Probe 4 to 3 (spread condition, tightened to require an open gap at the end); a run takes 1.7 s; identical hashes.

With partition and service rows seeded for the priority tables the real planning gate returns no decision at all (nothing blocks planning: the seed's own leader replica satisfies the priority partition and priority recovery bypasses the settling wait), so the lease-wait observations the live signature carries (1002 waits) do not come from priority-partition rebalancers on scenario rows; they need the real bootstrap and publication flow (nodes joining with incomplete leases, publications) that later slices host. Charging by real turn counts makes readiness the seed's heaviest owner here (7020 segments at 1.88 ms = 62 percent busy) because the live calibration's readiness segments are rare and heavy; whether simulated turn counts match live ones is the fidelity question the coefficient sweep answers.

Verifier (subagent): APPROVE on the planning-path seam batch (hunks A-G: rebalancer policy scheduler, planning gate, priority readiness, critical topology, both recovery-coordinator constructions, readiness version key, watchdog registry clock) - this/rebalancer binding proven through the mixin composition, byte-identical defaults, red-on-revert reasoned against HEAD (the start-delay gate's Date.now default rejects the awaited pass), 13 suites green (239 assertions), lint and guideline audits clean. The two hunks it flagged as outside the list are seams 2a and 2b, approved earlier and committed on quest/formation-sim-seams. Stale JSDoc on getTimeUntilRebalanceStartEligible fixed.

Publish gate caught what the verifier's reasoning missed: test/control-plane/priority-recovery-projection-brand-short-circuit builds a partial readiness host below the participation base, so this.now is absent there and the version-key seam threw; the seam now falls back to the key's own default when the host has no clock. The cheap gates (fast static, hook) cannot see this class of miss; only the change proof can.

Second gate-caught partial host: test/rebalancer/runtime-service-affinity-policy-lift composes the policy-scheduler mixin onto a bare PolicyHost without nowFn. Instead of patching sites one by one, the shared bag gains ownerNowMs(host) - the host's nowFn when present, the ambient clock otherwise - and every planning-path seam site routes through it; 265 rebalancer and readiness suites green locally before the republish. Lesson for the cheap-checks rule: for a seam that touches a mixin, run the whole owner directory's suites before publishing, not only the suites the verifier picked.

After the seams landed and the seed's owner passes are charged by real turn counts, LifeRaft moves every priority group's leadership off the seed onto joiners during formation (seed 62 percent busy, heartbeats late, followers time out and elect): the simulator reproduces the frozen-seed leadership migration the harness notes as CL-039 without any harness decision. The slice test now asserts only that every group has a leader; which node leads is Raft's own outcome under the charged clock and is recorded as data in formationMetrics.groups.

Owner amendments 2026-09-14 change a sealed constraint, so this quest is superseded rather than reinterpreted (R09). The sealed statement and the not-tuned-by-construction constraint require the signature to hold at every point of the 0.5x-2x sweep; the owner's amendment 8 replaces that with a sensitivity rule, where 1.0x reproduces the sealed signature and perturbed points must preserve the causal and failure classification rather than identical numbers. Three further amendments add contract the statement does not carry: worker_dispatch is observed-inactive with no measured mean and must fail closed rather than cost zero, the charging unit is dispatchCount + handoffCount so a synchronous runFormationOwner handoff costs one destination segment, and scheduler causality is an explicit invariant with a falsifier. The work stands and continues under the replacement; the design note in solve/epics/formation-seed-decoupling/design.md carries all ten amendments, committed as 1c9f62017.
